next_issue.title: feat(space): programmatic space scope with variable consumption, auto-area calculation, and 30% circulation rule
next_issue.body:
### Overview
As part of debim v0.9.0 Wave 2, implement programmatic functional scopes in `IfcSpace` allowing spaces to consume declared furniture/equipment variables (`contains: [ref: ...]`), automatically compute minimum required net area using the architectural formula:
$$\text{Required Area} = \left(\sum \text{Footprint of Contained Items}\right) \times 1.30$$
and define design specifications for automated architectural unit testing.

### Tasks
1. In `src/debim/schema.py`: Update `IfcSpace` to support:
   - `contains: Optional[List[VariableReference]] = None`
   - `design_spec: Optional[SpaceDesignSpec] = None` with fields: `min_area`, `clear_height`, `natural_ventilation_ratio`, `adjacencies` (must_connect, forbidden_adjacent).
2. In `src/debim/resolver.py`: Resolve variable references inside spaces, compute bounding areas with clearance envelopes, and calculate `required_net_area` with the 30% intra-room circulation multiplier.
3. Add unit tests in `tests/test_space_functional_scope.py` verifying automated area calculation from contained items.

### Acceptance Criteria
- `IfcSpace` correctly consumes variable references and computes required net area.
- `pytest tests/test_space_functional_scope.py` passes 100%.
next_issue.label: jules

next_issue.title: feat(solver): fast pre-flight 2D geometric furniture fit solver and non-overlapping clearance checking
next_issue.body:
### Overview
As part of debim v0.9.0 Wave 3, create a fast pre-flight 2D geometric fit solver that verifies whether all declared furniture envelopes fit inside a space polygon without overlapping or blocking walkways before drafting physical walls and columns.

### Tasks
1. Create `src/debim/solver.py`: Implement pure-Python / NumPy 2D Bounding Box packing and Separating Axis Theorem (SAT) collision detection for furniture footprints + human activity clearance envelopes.
2. In `src/debim/cli.py`: Expose command `debim fit -m <project_file>` returning instant Pass/Fail and placement coordinates for each piece of furniture.
3. Verify walkway path connectivity (minimum 0.60m corridor) between the space entrance and each functional envelope.
4. Add unit tests in `tests/test_furniture_fit_solver.py`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly identifies undersized spaces where furniture envelopes clash or exceed boundaries in < 0.01s.
- `pytest tests/test_furniture_fit_solver.py` passes 100%.
next_issue.label: jules

next_issue.title: feat(compliance): 5-layer architectural and engineering audit matrix, structured remediation, and audit flight recorder (debim audit)
next_issue.body:
### Overview
As part of debim v0.9.0 Wave 4, turn architectural design criteria, Thai building regulations, structural load path rules, and MEP flows into an automated 5-Layer Audit Matrix (`debim audit` / `debim test`), with actionable structured remediation plans and an Audit Flight Recorder (`audit_log.json`, `audit_report.md`) for continuous engine telemetry.

### Tasks
1. In `src/debim/compliance.py` & `src/debim/audit.py`: Implement the 5-Layer Audit Matrix:
   - Layer 1: Spatial & Functional (Net area >= min_area, furniture clearance non-overlap SAT, 2.60m+ clear head-room)
   - Layer 2: Legal & Life Safety (Thai Building Act MR 55: natural vent >= 10%, bathroom slab drop <= -0.10m, stair riser <= 0.20m & tread >= 0.22m, egress corridors >= 1.00m)
   - Layer 3: Structural Integrity (Column continuous vertical stack, beam supporting walls, roof-to-ground load path)
   - Layer 4: MEP Continuity & Gravity (Sanitary drain slope >= 1:100, vent stacks to exterior, electrical home runs)
   - Layer 5: Constructability & Physical Clashes (Zero hard clashes between Arch, Struct, MEP)
2. Provide Actionable Structured Remediation with machine-readable auto-fix proposals (`fix_action: 'EXPAND_SPACE' | 'ADD_WINDOW' | 'SHIFT_COLUMN' | 'RE_ROUTE_PIPE'`).
3. Implement Audit Flight Recorder in `src/debim/flight_recorder.py` exporting `audit_log.json` and human-readable `audit_report.md`.
4. In `src/debim/cli.py`: Expose `debim audit -m <project.debim> [--fix] [--log-dir <dir>]`.
5. Add unit tests in `tests/test_architectural_compliance.py` and `tests/test_audit_matrix.py`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- `debim audit` flags violations across all 5 layers with structured remediation suggestions.
- Telemetry correctly writes `audit_log.json` with timestamped diagnostics and remediation status.
- `pytest tests/test_architectural_compliance.py` and `pytest tests/test_audit_matrix.py` pass 100%.
next_issue.label: jules

next_issue.title: feat(derive): touching spaces relative syntax and automated structural derivation engine (debim derive)
next_issue.body:
### Overview
As part of debim v0.9.0 Wave 5 (Final Wave), enable AI and architects to model by declaring simply how spaces touch each other (`touching: { target, side, align }`) and implement the `debim derive` auto-framing engine that derives walls, doors, windows, columns, and beams automatically from touching space boundaries.

### Tasks
1. In `src/debim/schema.py`: Support relative space placement via `touching: { target: str, side: Literal['NORTH', 'SOUTH', 'EAST', 'WEST'], align: Optional[Literal['LEFT', 'RIGHT', 'CENTER', 'TOP', 'BOTTOM']] }`.
2. Create `src/debim/derive.py`:
   - Shared touching boundary between 2 spaces -> internal `IfcWall`.
   - Exterior boundary -> exterior `IfcWall` + `IfcWindow`.
   - `must_connect` spaces -> centered `IfcDoor`.
   - Touching corner vertices -> `IfcColumn`.
   - Wall baselines -> `IfcBeam` and `IfcSlab`.
3. In `src/debim/cli.py`: Expose command `debim derive -m <floorplan.debim> -o <project.debim>`.
4. Provide `examples/architectural_tdd_house/`: A full 250+ element benchmark project generated from touching spaces passing 100% of architectural unit tests.
5. Add unit tests in `tests/test_touching_spaces.py`, `tests/test_derive_engine.py`, and `tests/test_architectural_tdd_benchmark.py`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- `debim derive` converts relative touching spaces into complete structural and architectural BIM elements.
- The benchmark project compiles cleanly to IFC4 and passes `debim test`.
- `pytest tests/` passes 100%.
next_issue.label: jules
